title: Automated Credit Card Due Reminder Notification
testDescription: Validate that an automated credit card due reminder notification is correctly generated, sent to the cardholder, and displays only the last 4 digits of the card number.
prerequisites: Cardholder has an active credit card account with an upcoming payment due; valid contact information on file; account is not overdue.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer and access scheduled notifications dashboard. 2. Select cardholder account with upcoming due date. 3. Simulate system-generated due reminder trigger. 4. Review content draft of notification for accuracy. 5. Verify masked card number shows only last 4 digits. 6. Confirm notification delivery to cardholder's email/SMS. 7. Cardholder receives notification and checks content. 8. Cardholder verifies presence of masked card identifier and due date. 9. Check audit log for notification trigger and delivery timestamp.
expectedResult: Due reminder notification is sent on schedule; notification displays last 4 digits of card; full card number is not present; audit trail records delivery; cardholder verifies correct content.
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking enforced, audit trail logged
timingVerification: Notification sent 5 days before due date
ASSUMPTION: Due reminder trigger interval set as 5 days before due

title: Overdue Balance Alert with Boundary Amount and Escalation
testDescription: Test the overdue balance alert notification for an account at escalation threshold, ensuring only last 4 digits of credit card are shown and escalation triggers are correct.
prerequisites: Cardholder missed payment deadline; account balance exactly at escalation threshold; overdue status in system.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer and locate account with overdue status at threshold value. 2. Trigger overdue balance alert. 3. Review notification content for overdue amount, escalation risks, and card identifier. 4. Verify card number masking (last 4 digits only). 5. Confirm notification is sent promptly to cardholder. 6. Cardholder checks notification and identifies masked card. 7. Confirm escalation trigger is enabled for collection workflow. 8. Review audit trail for overdue alert, content, and mask status. 9. Check system logs for correct overdue threshold boundary processing.
expectedResult: Overdue alert is sent promptly; only last 4 digits appear in message; escalation workflow transitions as expected; audit logs show proper masking and delivery.
ASSUMPTION: Escalation threshold defined by business rules

title: PII Masking Enforcement Across All Notifications
testDescription: Verify negative scenarios where full credit card number is accidentally exposed in any UI, notification, or integration, ensuring system blocks and reports such incidents.
prerequisites: System prepared to send collection notifications; cardholder with significant delinquency; admin can inject faulty data for test.
stepsToPerform: 1. Inject test notification template with unmasked/full card number. 2. Attempt to send notification (email, SMS, letter) to cardholder. 3. Review notification content preview in UI. 4. Check system's masking enforcement logic and validation. 5. Attempt notification delivery to external collection agency. 6. Validate that system blocks delivery of unmasked card number. 7. Review error messages and incident reports generated. 8. Examine audit logs for failed notification, masking check, and escalation handling. 9. Verify that no UI screens, emails, or integrations display full card number.
expectedResult: System blocks any notification with full card number; errors reported; audit trail shows masking validation failure; no communication with full card number sent.

title: Payment Plan Proposal Workflow and Reversal
testDescription: Validate the structured payment plan proposal workflow: eligibility calculation, notification, acceptance, cancellation, content including last 4 digits, and audit trail.
prerequisites: Cardholder with overdue and escalated balance; issuer enabled for payment plan proposals; system defines plan eligibility rules.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer, locate eligible overdue account. 2. Trigger payment plan proposal workflow. 3. Review generated proposal content for schedule, rates, masked card number. 4. Cardholder receives proposal notification (email/SMS). 5. Cardholder reviews proposal, verifies masked card identifier, and accepts plan. 6. Monitor workflow transition to 'payment plan' state. 7. Cardholder initiates cancellation request for payment plan. 8. System processes cancellation, reverts account to prior state. 9. Review audit log for proposal, acceptance, reversal, and content masking.
expectedResult: Payment plan proposal delivered with masked card number; acceptance and cancellation handled properly; workflow states and masking logged; no unmasked PII exposure; audit shows full journey.
ASSUMPTION: Payment plan can be cancelled or reverted

title: Full Credit Card Collections Journey with Multi-Role Escalation
testDescription: End-to-end test spanning due reminder, overdue alert, collection notification, payment plan, agency escalation, legal action; ensure notifications, masking, state transitions, and audit comply.
prerequisites: Cardholder with active credit card; issuer and collection agency roles; overdue payment, escalation, and legal action thresholds defined; system audit enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Cardholder receives due reminder (masked card identifier). 2. Cardholder misses payment; system sends overdue alert (masked). 3. Account escalates; issuer sends formal collection notice (masked). 4. Cardholder is offered payment plan proposal (masked); cardholder declines. 5. Issuer triggers handover to collection agency; agency receives masked card digits only. 6. Collection agency initiates communications (masked identifier). 7. Cardholder fails to respond; issuer initiates legal action and sends documentation (masked). 8. All role-based actions validated for permissions and access. 9. Each notification, escalation, and transition recorded in audit log with masking verification.
expectedResult: All notifications, alerts, escalations, and communications show only last 4 digits; state transitions logged; audit trails present for each step; no unmasked PII exposed; regulatory compliance throughout.
workflowSteps: due reminder → overdue → collection → payment plan → agency → legal
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking, state transitions, audit, multi-role access
timingAndAlertingVerification: each step occur at correct interval
ASSUMPTION: Full cross-role journey enabled and tracked via audit

title: Simultaneous Overdue Alerts for Multiple Cards per Cardholder
testDescription: Validate system behavior when a single cardholder has multiple credit cards overdue on the same day, ensuring separate notifications are sent for each account with correct last 4 digit masking and audit logging.
prerequisites: Cardholder holds two or more credit cards; each card past due date; overdue amounts and account statuses defined.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer and retrieve cardholder profile with multiple cards. 2. Set both cards to overdue status in system. 3. Trigger overdue notification batch process. 4. Review generated notifications for each card. 5. Confirm each notification contains correct masked last 4 digits for the respective cards. 6. Cardholder receives multiple notifications and verifies masked card identifiers. 7. Check audit log for notification triggers, delivery, and masking validation per card. 8. Ensure no cross-contamination of card details in content. 9. Validate prompt and independent delivery of all alerts.
expectedResult: Separate overdue notifications sent for each overdue card; only the last 4 digits of each respective card displayed; audit logs show independent triggers and masking verification; no full card number or cross-account data revealed.
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking, multi-account segregation, audit trail
ASSUMPTION: Cardholder can possess multiple cards; system supports batch overdue notifications.

title: Unauthorized Collection Agency Access Attempt
testDescription: Ensure collection agencies cannot access or trigger credit card notifications or view credit card account data unless the issuer has completed formal handover and audit records are established.
prerequisites: Cardholder account is overdue, but handover to collection agency has not occurred; agency user attempts access.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as collection agency user. 2. Attempt to list overdue cardholder accounts in issuer system. 3. Try accessing communication templates and notifications for delinquent cardholders. 4. Attempt viewing detailed account and card information prior to handover. 5. Observe UI screens, emails, and API responses. 6. Validate system permission logic enforces access restrictions. 7. Check audit logs for access attempt and security event recording. 8. Confirm that only masked last 4 digits (if any) are visible and no full card data or account details shown. 9. Issue negative test report for unauthorized access.
expectedResult: Collection agency user blocked from accessing overdue accounts and communications before handover; audit log records attempt; no card information, even masked, is revealed until proper state transition; regulatory compliance maintained.
ASSUMPTION: Issuer system enforces access controls and tracks unauthorized activity.

title: Irreversible Escalation to Legal Action and Audit Trail
testDescription: Validate irreversible workflow transition when issuer initiates legal action after collection agency cycle, ensuring documentation, audit, and masked card identifier are handled according to regulatory standards.
prerequisites: Cardholder account escalated through agency; legal action threshold met; issuer authorized for legal escalation.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer; verify account qualifies for legal escalation. 2. Initiate legal action workflow and trigger formal documentation generation. 3. Verify legal notification content includes only last 4 digits of card. 4. Send legal notification to cardholder and legal participant. 5. Ensure account state changes to 'legal escalation' and cannot revert. 6. Legal role attempts to access account history and communications. 7. Review audit log for legal action initiation, content masking, and state transition. 8. Confirm compliance checks for PII masking and audit documentation. 9. Attempt reversal and validate system blocks workflow change; review audit block event.
expectedResult: Legal action workflow triggers irreversibly; legal documentation and communications display only last 4 digits; audit trail captures escalation; PII masking maintained; reversal attempts logged and blocked.
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking, audit, irreversibility, legal documentation
ASSUMPTION: Legal action state is business-critical and cannot be undone.

title: Credit Card Collection Notification with Cross-Role Review
testDescription: Validate collection notification workflow: issuer generates and sends formal collection notice, content reviewed both by issuer and cardholder, ensuring only masked last 4 digits are present and audit log complete.
prerequisites: Account is significantly delinquent; overdue balance exceeds collection threshold; issuer and cardholder with required permissions.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer; locate account flagged for collection. 2. Generate formal collection notification. 3. Review notification content and masked card identifier in issuer UI. 4. Send notification to cardholder via email/SMS. 5. Cardholder receives notice and reviews masked identifier. 6. Both issuer and cardholder review audit history of the collection workflow. 7. Verify no unmasked card numbers are visible on any screen or in notification. 8. Validate timing of notification is in accordance with escalation policies. 9. Regenerate notification and verify audit log appends new event with masking check.
expectedResult: Collection notification sent with correct content and masked identifier; issuer and cardholder can verify audit trail; all communications comply with masking standards; notification timing matches policy.
ASSUMPTION: Both issuer and cardholder must have audit access.

title: Payment Plan Eligibility and Alert Override Validation
testDescription: Test decision-table calculations for payment plan eligibility, automatic alert overrides for non-eligible accounts, and enforce last 4 digit masking in all communications.
prerequisites: Multiple overdue accounts; system rules for payment plan eligibility defined; issuer role with override ability.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer; access overdue accounts dashboard. 2. Select accounts with varying overdue balances and payment histories. 3. Trigger payment plan proposal workflow for each account. 4. System calculates eligibility based on decision table (balance, history, prior plans). 5. System automatically overrides alert for non-eligible accounts and sends rejection notification. 6. Review all notifications (proposals, rejections) for correct masking of card numbers. 7. Cardholders receive notifications and verify masked identifiers. 8. Audit log records each eligibility calculation, alert override, and masking check. 9. Validate issuer override action triggers correct notification and audit event.
expectedResult: Payment plan proposal sent only to eligible accounts with masked card identifiers; non-eligible receive masked rejection alert; decision table and audit logs confirm correct calculations and masking enforcement.
stateTransition: overdue → payment plan attempt → eligible or rejected
regulatoryComplianceCheck: decision table logic, masking, audit, alert override
ASSUMPTION: Issuer can override on exceptional cases; system calculates eligibility per business rules.

title: Payment Plan Cancellation at Boundary State after Partial Payment
testDescription: Validate system behavior when a cardholder requests payment plan cancellation after completing a partial payment, ensuring correct state transition, notification content, masked identifier, and audit integrity.
prerequisites: Cardholder enrolled in payment plan; partial payment completed; issuer allows plan cancellation per policy; account status updated.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as cardholder; view active payment plan details. 2. Complete partial payment towards plan (verify successful transaction). 3. Initiate payment plan cancellation request in UI. 4. Issuer receives cancellation request and reviews eligibility (boundary condition: partial payment, not full). 5. Trigger cancellation workflow; system recalculates account status. 6. System generates cancellation notification to cardholder (includes masked last 4 digits). 7. Cardholder receives notification and verifies masked identifier. 8. System moves account from 'payment plan' to 'delinquent' or 'overdue' state as per policy. 9. Audit log records partial payment, cancellation trigger, notification delivery, and masking check.
expectedResult: Payment plan is cancelled as requested; cancellation notification shows only last 4 digits of card; partial payment and cancellation recorded in audit log; account state reverts correctly; regulatory masking enforced.
stateTransition: payment plan → partial payment → cancellation → delinquent/overdue
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking, audit on partial payment, cancellation workflow
ASSUMPTION: Issuer policy permits plan cancellation after partial payment; system recalculates balance accordingly

title: Collection Agency Communication and Audit Trail Validation
testDescription: Validate automated collection agency communication process, ensuring only masked card number is shared, communication audit trail is created for each event, and state transitions are properly logged.
prerequisites: Issuer completed agency handover; agency user authorized for account communication; account flagged as escalated.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as collection agency user; view handover accounts. 2. Select account for communication initiation. 3. Generate agency communication (letter/email/SMS) for overdue balance. 4. Review content for correct masking of card number (last 4 digits only). 5. Send communication to cardholder. 6. Cardholder receives agency communication and verifies masked identifier. 7. Agency user accesses audit log for account—verify each communication event logged with masking check. 8. Attempt to regenerate or edit message templates and check for masking enforcement. 9. Confirm correct state transition from issuer handover to active agency status.
expectedResult: Agency communications always display only last 4 digits; all communications and edits logged in audit; state transitioned from issuer to agency; regulatory compliance on masking and audit.
stateTransition: issuer → collection agency → active agency communication
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking, communication audit logging, state transition
ASSUMPTION: Agency can only access post-handover accounts; all comms and edits audited

title: Erroneous Collection Notification Recurrence for Closed Account
testDescription: Test negative scenario where collection notification is triggered for an account that has been closed and paid in full, ensuring system blocks notification, enforces masking, and records incident in audit.
prerequisites: Account status set to 'closed' after full payment; issuer communication dashboard active; notification recurrence job enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer; list closed accounts. 2. Simulate recurrence job for collection notifications (system error injection). 3. Attempt to trigger collection notification for closed account. 4. System checks eligibility and blocks notification sending. 5. Verify no communication template generated (UI/email/SMS) for closed account. 6. Review system error messages and audit events for recurrence block. 7. Ensure audit trail explicitly records blocked notification and account status. 8. Attempt to override and manually send notification—system blocks. 9. Validate that no card number (masked or otherwise) appears in blocked communications.
expectedResult: System blocks erroneous collection notifications for closed accounts; audit log records blocked event; no communications, masked or unmasked, sent; regulatory masking and account status checks enforced.
regulatoryComplianceCheck: account status validation, masking, notification eligibility audit
ASSUMPTION: Closed accounts cannot receive collection notifications; system audits all blocked attempts

title: Overdue Amount Recalculation with Edge Case: Multiple Overdue Accounts and Partial Payments
testDescription: Validate overdue alert calculation logic when cardholder has multiple overdue cards with partial payments posted on different accounts, ensuring notifications reflect correct balances, masked identifiers, and audit trail integrity.
prerequisites: Cardholder with two overdue credit cards; partial payments posted to each account in varying amounts; issuer alert system enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as issuer; retrieve cardholder profile with multiple overdue accounts. 2. Post partial payments to each account (different values). 3. System recalculates overdue amounts for each account. 4. Trigger overdue alert batch for all cardholder overdue accounts. 5. Review notification content for each account—correct masked last 4 digits and recalculated overdue balance. 6. Cardholder receives multiple alerts and verifies masked identifiers and values. 7. Check audit logs for recalculation event, masking verification, and alert delivery per card. 8. Ensure no cross-account data appears in any notification. 9. Validate prompt, independent alerts and audit trails for all actions.
expectedResult: Separate overdue alerts sent for each account with recalculated balances; each notification contains correct masked last 4 digits; audit trail logs recalculation and alert for all accounts; no cross-account contamination.
regulatoryComplianceCheck: overdue recalculation, masking, audit, multi-account separation
ASSUMPTION: Partial payments trigger real-time recalculation and alerts for each card

title: Legal Action Initiation with Role-Based UI and Masked Documentation Download
testDescription: Validate legal action workflow: legal participant logs into system, accesses account flagged for legal action, reviews all communications, downloads legal documentation with only masked last 4 digits displayed, and verifies audit log.
prerequisites: Issuer escalated account to legal action; legal role assigned; document generation policy enabled; account status 'legal'; audit logging active.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login as legal participant; access UI dashboard for legal action accounts. 2. Select account flagged as 'legal' for review. 3. Open communication history and verify all previously sent notifications display only last 4 digits. 4. Initiate legal documentation download; review content for masking policy (only last 4 digits, never full card number). 5. Review timing and content accuracy of legal notifications in UI. 6. Attempt to download multiple documentation files and verify masking consistently enforced. 7. Review audit log for download event, masking verification, and role-based access. 8. Attempt to view/edit card data—system blocks unmasked full number display. 9. Validate legal role audit event records for each action (view, download, attempted edit).
expectedResult: Legal participant access limited to masked card identifier only; all communications and documentation show only last 4 digits; audit trail covers all accesses, downloads, and masking validation; regulatory compliance on data handling.
stateTransition: collection agency → legal action → documentation download
regulatoryComplianceCheck: PII masking, role-based access, audit log, legal documentation
ASSUMPTION: Legal participants have read/download access but never edit/view full card number
